faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a solid fuel burning device or gas
               burning device which has not been approved during a high pollution day unless an exemption
               has been granted as hereinafter provided. It shall be the duty of all persons owning
               or operating a solid fuel burning device or an unapproved gas burning device to be
               aware of a declaration by the state department of health of a high pollution day.
(b)
At the time of a declaration of a high pollution day by the state department of health,
               the city manager shall allow three hours for the burndown of existing fires in solid
               fuel burning devices prior to commencement of enforcement of this article.
(c)
It shall be unlawful for any person to install a fireplace or gas burning device within
               a new building or a building being remodeled or renovated which does not meet the
               most stringent emission performance requirements of the U.S. Environmental Protection
               Agency or state statute regulations promulgated by the State Air Quality Control Commission
               as of July 1, 1990.
(d)
Visible emissions limitation: No person shall cause or allow a visible emission from
               any wood-burning device in any building or structure that exceeds 20 percent opacity
               for a period or periods aggregating more than six consecutive minutes in any one-hour
               period. Visible emissions from the startup of a new fire for a period not to exceed
               twenty consecutive minutes in any consecutive four-hour period are not subject to
               this provision.
(e)
Determination of visible emissions: The approved reference test method for visible
               emission measurement is EPA Method 9 (Visual Determination of the Opacity of Emissions
               from Stationary Sources, 40 CFR, Part 60 Appendix A-July 1992).
(f)
Prohibition against burning garbage, non-seasoned wood or certain materials: No person
               shall cause or allow any of the following materials to be burned in a wood-burning
               device: garbage, treated wood, non-seasoned wood, used or contaminated wood pallets,
               plastic products, rubber products, waste petroleum products, paints and paint solvents,
               particle board, and any material not intended by a manufacturer for use as a fuel
               in a wood-burning device.
(Code 1981, § 21-77; Ord. No. 2451, § 1, 10-19-1987; Ord. No. 2868, § § 8, 9, 1-20-1992;
Ord. No. 4151, § 2, 12-15-2008
